A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

inflation is possible for the scalar electrodynamics model and for the $SU(2) \otimes SU(3)$ model, and that the corresponding values of coupling function are positive, while for the finite $U(1)$ gauge model and the $SU(3) \otimes U(1)$ model, the coupling function has to be negative, which is not acceptable.

, in order to construct inflationary potentials from the RG-improved potentials of scalar electrodynamics, $SU(2)_{L}$, or $SU(5)_{L}\times SU(5)_{R}$, one needs a positive coupling function, which corresponds to an unstable de Sitter solution.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the $SU(2) \times U(1)$ and $SU(N)_{c}$ models, the tree-level inflationary potential, which corresponds in the Einstein frame to the cosmological term, is non-viable for inflation.
